newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - cash firmer after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - cash firmer after jobs data.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds firmed in early trade after April employment data showed a lower-than-expected increase in non-farm payrolls, but the lowest jobless rate since 1973.
"The numbers look pretty good," one trader said. "The unemployment rate was lower than expected, but the gross number was good. The hourly earnings looked good.

The Labor Department said non-farm payrolls increased by 142,000 in April, lower than the 211,000 increase economists polled by Reuters forecasted on average. The jobless rate however fell to 4.9 percent, its lowest level in 23 years.
"They were still expecting it to stay up with a five handle on it," a trader said.
The trader said while the market was up 1/4 to 3/8 of a point shortly after the number, gauging levels was difficult given the municipal bond contract's volatility.

"Certainly the first 15 to 30 minutes after the data, the contract jumps around so much it's very hard to make an offering," the trader said. "I would say just by cuffing it looking at the contract, looking at where people have bumped their offerings, I'd say the market is up 1/4 to 3/8."
A second trader said the market appeared slightly firmer than Thursday's closing levels, but that players remained cautious.

"A couple of quotes out there were all firmer right around the number, and after the number," the second trader said. "Stuff like San Antonio (electric and gas) 5s of '12 traded at a 5.51. Yesterday they traded at a 5.55."
The second trader also cited futures market volatility.
"I think the futures contract has people a little leery right now, you know it went up 18, 19 ticks right away, came back in, went back up and now we are back to close to unchanged."
Closer to 1000 EDT, the June municipal contract was up 8/32 at 114-30/32. The June T-bond contract was up 7/32 at 109-28/32. The MOB spread was 162 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 2/32 at 96-13/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
Looking ahead to next week, traders cited a large calendar. The largest negotiated deal is expected to be a $486 mllion San Antonio electric and gas deal via PaineWebber Inc.
